claims.text: The random-solid-solution HfNbTaTiZr alloy has severe lattice distortion arising from atomic-size mismatch and random chemical distribution.
Monte Carlo-based equilibration can produce chemical short-range order relative to a random solid solution.
Monte Carlo treatment of HfNbTaTiZr will specifically promote HfTi and TiZr binary clusters and percolating networks.
Annealing or controlled cooling can evolve the HfTi/TiZr short-range order into ordered B2-like structures.
Formation of SRO, percolating binary clusters, and B2-like order will increase the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr relative to its random solid solution.
B2-like ordering reduces local lattice-distortion, atomic-mass-environment, and bond-stiffness fluctuations relative to the random state.
Random alloys strongly scatter phonons through mass variance and strain-field fluctuations.
Ordered B2-like clusters provide a more periodic potential for high-frequency phonons, reducing their scattering rate and increasing their relaxation time.
Percolation of low-distortion ordered regions creates low-resistance pathways for high-frequency phonon transport.
AlCoFeNi can form a single ordered B2 phase after annealing at 1000 °C for 15 hours.
B2-like ordering is implied in the Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy system by the cited evidence.
SRO impedes dislocation motion and strengthens MoNbTaW relative to its random solid solution at low temperature.
The relevant transport regime is approximately 300–800 K, where phonon-phonon scattering is significant but does not dominate defect scattering.
High-frequency phonon modes in the ordered state will have narrower linewidths and longer lifetimes than in the random state.
The conductivity increase will be largest at 300–600 K because defect scattering dominates over Umklapp scattering in that interval.
Small or isolated non-percolating SRO clusters will act as scattering centers and decrease lattice thermal conductivity.
A conductivity increase requires either a percolating ordered network or a significant reduction in local lattice-distortion variance.
Incoherent ordered phases or B2/matrix lattice mismatch can create strain fields sufficient to reverse the proposed conductivity increase.
The random HfNbTaTiZr solid solution typically has low thermal conductivity because of lattice-distortion and mass-variance scattering.
Relative phonon linewidths, atomic displacement parameters, high-frequency phonon DOS features, and lattice thermal conductivity can discriminate between reduced scattering and increased distortion.
